blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario A's snapshot id begins 4f1e. A planner copies A to a new scenario B and changes nothing. Later she sets B's relative gap tolerance from 0 to 0.01. Following the lesson, what is B's snapshot id right after the copy, and after the change?

options.text: New right after the copy, since every copy is a new scenario
options.says: The id hashes the inputs, not the name: cut-2029 had the base's id until its budget changed.

options.text: Equal to A's both times, since no data value was changed
options.says: The solver settings are part of the inputs the snapshot hashes, so changing the gap tolerance changes the id.

options.text: New after the copy, and back to A's once the tolerance changes
options.says: A copy with identical inputs has the same id; a changed setting can only make it differ from A's.

options.text: Equal to A's after the copy, and new once the tolerance changes
options.says: Right: equal inputs give the same id, and the settings are part of the inputs.

origin.section: A Scenario Is a Copy With Its Own Snapshot, Never an Edit of Another Scenario

questions.stem: In Post-Opt, a planner learns that project W7, which the run left out, was promised to a town council, and wants it in the plan. Following the lesson's cycle, what happens next?

options.text: W7 is added to the plan by hand, and the run's NPV is kept
options.says: That is a plan no run produced: it could overspend, and its NPV would be a number no solver computed.

options.text: W7 is forced in, the scenario returns to Pre-Opt, and is rerun
options.says: Right: an override is a change of inputs, so it gets a new snapshot, returns to Pre-Opt and needs a rerun.

options.text: The plan is locked first, and W7 is then added to the locked plan
options.says: A locked scenario refuses edits; a change after lock needs a copy.

options.text: The request is refused, since planners may never change the inputs
options.says: Planners change inputs in Pre-Opt; the lesson's planner forces P024 in.

origin.section: Post-Opt Reads the Plan, and Every Override Sends the Scenario Back for a Rerun

questions.stem: A week after Budget Lock, finance learns that the 2030 budget will be $500k lower than the one in the plan of record. Following the lesson, what happens to the locked scenario?

options.text: Its 2030 budget is edited, and it is rerun in place
options.says: A locked scenario refuses edits: the lesson's attempt to edit it was refused.

options.text: It is unlocked, edited, rerun and locked once more
options.says: Budget Lock is never left; the stage table says changes go to a copy.

options.text: It stays as it is, and a copy carries the new budget
options.says: Right: a change after lock needs a copy, which goes through the cycle and, if adopted, replaces the plan of record by a decision.

options.text: It is deleted, since its budget no longer holds
options.says: The plan of record is kept with its snapshot and plan, so nobody has to re-derive it.

origin.section: Budget Lock Freezes the Plan of Record, and a Change Means a New Scenario
